# 1 Maccabees Chapter 3 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_003_page_001.jpg

---

1. Then his son Judas, who was called Maccabeus, took his place.
2. All his brothers and all who had joined his father gave him their support, and they gladly fought for Israel.
3. He extended his people's glory. He put on a breastplate like a giant and belted on his weapons of war. He set battles in order and shielded the host with his sword.
4. In his acts he was like a lion, and like a young lion roaring for its prey.
5. He hunted down and sought out those who broke the law, and burned those who troubled his people.
6. The lawless shrank back for fear of him; all the evildoers were thrown into confusion; and deliverance prospered by his hand.
7. He brought grief to many kings and gladness to Jacob with his deeds; his memory is blessed forever.
8. He went throughout the cities of Judah, destroying the ungodly from among them and turning away wrath from Israel.
9. His fame spread to the ends of the earth, and he rallied those who were perishing.
10. Apollonius gathered together the Gentiles and a great and powerful force from Samaria to make war against Israel.
11. When Judas learned of it, he went out to meet him. He defeated and killed him, and many were killed; the survivors fled.
12. They took their plunder, and Judas took the sword of Apollonius, and with it he fought all his days.
13. When Seron, the commander of the Syrian army, heard that Judas had gathered an assembly of faithful men with him — a congregation ready for war —
14. he said, "I will win fame and honor in the kingdom by making war on Judas and his followers, who have defied the king's command."
15. A strong force of lawless men came up with him to help him, to take vengeance on the Israelites.
16. As he approached the ascent of Beth-horon, Judas went out to meet him with a small company.
17. When the men saw the army coming against them, they said to Judas: "How can we, so few as we are, fight such a great and powerful multitude? We are exhausted — we have eaten nothing today."
18. Judas replied: "It is easy for many to be hemmed in by few, and in the sight of Heaven there is no difference between deliverance by many or by few.
19. Victory in war does not depend on the size of the fighting force, but strength comes from Heaven.
20. They come against us in great insolence and lawlessness to destroy us, our wives and our children, and to plunder us.
21. But we fight for our lives and our laws.
22. God himself will crush them before us; do not be afraid of them."
23. When he had finished speaking, he charged them suddenly, and Seron and his army were routed before him.
24. He pursued them down the descent of Beth-horon to the plain. About eight hundred of them fell, and the rest fled into the land of the Philistines.
25. Then fear of Judas and his brothers fell upon all the surrounding nations. His fame reached the king, and every nation spoke of the battles of Judas.
26. When King Antiochus heard these reports, he was filled with rage. He sent out orders and gathered all the forces of his kingdom — an exceedingly strong army.
27. He opened his treasury and gave his forces a year's pay, ordering them to be prepared for any requirement.
28. But he saw that the money in his treasury was running low and that the tribute from the region was meager, due to the strife and disaster he had brought on the land by abolishing the customs that had been in place from the earliest times.
29. He was afraid that he would not have enough — as he had before — for his expenses and the gifts he used to give with a lavish hand, more lavishly than the kings before him.
30. He was greatly troubled, and he resolved to go to Persia and collect tribute from those provinces and to raise a large sum of money.
31. He left behind Lysias, a distinguished man of royal blood, to oversee the king's affairs from the Euphrates River to the borders of Egypt,
32. and to raise his son Antiochus until his return.
33. He handed over to him half the forces and the elephants, and gave him instructions regarding all he wished done, especially concerning the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem:
34. he was to send an army against them to crush and uproot the strength of Israel and the remnant of Jerusalem, to blot out their memory from that place,
35. and to settle foreigners throughout their whole territory and distribute their land by lot.
36. The king took the remaining half of the forces and marched out from Antioch, his royal city, in the one hundred and forty-seventh year. He crossed the Euphrates River and advanced through the upper provinces.
37. Lysias chose Ptolemy son of Dorymenes, Nicanor, and Gorgias — powerful men among the king's Friends —
38. and sent with them forty thousand infantry and seven thousand cavalry to march into Judah and lay it waste, as the king had commanded.
39. They set out with all their forces, came and camped near Emmaus in the coastal plain.
40. The merchants of the region heard about them and came to the camp with very large amounts of silver and gold, along with fetters, planning to buy the Israelites as slaves. Forces from Syria and the foreign lands also joined them.
41. When Judas and his brothers saw that the situation was growing desperate and that enemy forces were encamped within their territory, and when they learned of the king's orders to destroy and utterly annihilate the people,
42. they said to one another: "Let us restore our people from their ruin and fight for our people and the sanctuary."
43. The assembly was gathered together to prepare for battle and to pray and beg for mercy and compassion.
44. Jerusalem was deserted like a wilderness; none of her children came in or went out. The sanctuary was trampled down and foreigners garrisoned the citadel, a lodging place for Gentiles. Joy had departed from Jacob; pipe and harp had fallen silent.
45. They gathered and went to Mizpah, opposite Jerusalem, for in former days there had been a place of prayer for Israel at Mizpah.
46. They fasted that day, put on sackcloth and sprinkled ashes on their heads, and tore their garments.
47. They spread out the Torah scrolls, the ones the Gentiles had used as patterns for painting the likenesses of their idols.
48. They brought the priestly vestments, the firstfruits, and the tithes; and they brought forward the Nazirites who had completed their vows.
49. They cried aloud toward Heaven: "What shall we do with these men, and where shall we bring them?
50. Your sanctuary has been trampled down and profaned; your priests are in mourning and humiliation.
51. And now the Gentiles are assembled against us to destroy us. You know what they intend against us.
52. How will we be able to stand against them, if you do not help us?"
53. Then they sounded the trumpets and cried out loudly.
54. After this Judas appointed leaders over the people: commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties, and commanders of tens.
55. He told all those who were building houses, or were betrothed, or were planting vineyards, or were fearful, to return home, according to the Torah.
56. Then the army moved on and camped south of Emmaus.
57. Judas said: "Arm yourselves and be brave men. In the morning be ready to fight these Gentiles who have assembled against us to destroy us and our sanctuary.
58. It is better for us to die in battle than to witness the destruction of our nation and the sanctuary.
59. But whatever the will of Heaven may be, so shall it be done."
60. Then Gorgias took five thousand infantry and a thousand picked cavalry, and this detachment moved out by night
